Can you explain the main options in simple terms?
• Just now
Seen • Just now
Here’s the simple version:
Whiskey — warm, rich, and often oaky; Bourbon tends toward vanilla and caramel, Rye is spicier, and Scotch can range from fruity to smoky.
Tequila — made from agave; bright and peppery when unaged, smoother and more vanilla-like when aged.
Rum — made from sugarcane or molasses; it can be light and tropical, or dark, rich, and spicy.
Gin — botanical and herbal, usually led by juniper; great for crisp, refreshing cocktails.
Vodka — clean and neutral; an easy starting point for mixing because it lets other flavors shine.
Brandy — fruit-based and often smooth, warming, and mellow.
Flaviar carries all of these categories, from familiar classics to craft and rare bottles.  Rum is especially broad, ranging from bright styles to richer, spicier pours.

Pour a small amount into any clean tumbler or glass.
Take a gentle smell, then a small sip—no need to rush.
Try it neat first so you can taste the Bourbon on its own. A tulip-shaped glass is ideal, but a regular whiskey tumbler works well too. 
If it feels too strong, add a small splash of water; this can soften the spice and bring out honey and vanilla notes.
If you prefer it cold, add one large ice cube rather than lots of small ones, so it chills without diluting too quickly.
